solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Some fancy a nice greenish-blue colour

indicators.note: 'some' of a phrase means only part of it, so the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: read straight through the end of fancy, the word a and the start of nice

explanation.surface: Someone admires a pleasant shade of blue-green.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyan is the name of the bright colour lying between green and blue on the spectrum.

clue.text: Grain, bivalve mollusc, and roadside plant

parts.note: corn is a cereal grain
a cockle is a small edible bivalve shellfish

explanation.surface: A list of things found in the countryside: cereal, shellfish and a wayside flower.
explanation.walkthrough: The list reads like three items, but the first two join to make the third.
explanation.definitionFit: The corncockle is a purple-flowered weed traditionally growing in cornfields and along verges.

clue.text: Check uranium in mine entrance

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: an adit is a horizontal passage into a mine
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: An inspector tests for radioactive ore at the mouth of a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: An audit is a formal inspection or examination, so as a verb it means to inspect.

clue.text: Wet blanket left with proceeds of robbery, say

parts.note: spoils are plunder, loot taken in robbery or war; 'say' marks robbery as just one source
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A gloomy person walks off with the stolen loot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left with' reads as abandoned holding, but the two pieces sit in reverse order of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A wet blanket is an idiom for someone who dampens others' fun, exactly a killjoy.

clue.text: Took part in parade, urged to protect commander

indicators.note: protecting something means surrounding it, so the outer word wraps round the inner

parts.note: to press someone is to urge them
CO is the abbreviation for commanding officer

explanation.surface: Soldiers marched in a parade, told to guard their commanding officer.
explanation.definitionFit: To process (stress on the second syllable) is to walk in a procession, so it means marched ceremonially.

clue.text: Leader of Italy no longer with us provided with inspiration

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of Italy
no longer with us is a euphemism for having died

explanation.surface: A late Italian head of state is remembered as a source of inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: IDEA'D is a rare dictionary form meaning furnished with an idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Having been given an idea is being provided with inspiration; the word is a past participle formed from idea.

clue.text: Furtiveness shown by duck in south

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

parts.note: STH is a standard abbreviation for south
the teal is a small duck

explanation.surface: A duck in the south of the country moves secretively.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealth means acting in a secret, quiet manner, the same quality as sneaky secretiveness.

clue.text: Practise too hard in cricket period, having a number of coaches

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket
a train is a string of railway carriages, called coaches

explanation.surface: A cricketer works too hard at the nets while several coaches look on.
explanation.walkthrough: Coaches here are railway carriages, not sports trainers.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtrain is to exercise or rehearse excessively, beyond what the body can recover from.

clue.text: Expression of disapproval over universal ballet wear

parts.note: tut is the clicking sound of mild disapproval
U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: Someone tuts at the costumes everyone wears in a ballet.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means the first piece sits above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutu is the short stiff skirt of layered net worn by ballerinas.

clue.text: Happen to live well at last, having crossed Cornish river

indicators.note: crossing something here means spanning it, so the outer letters straddle the river

parts.note: to be is to exist or live

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: the last letter of well
the Fal is a river in Cornwall, flowing into the sea at Falmouth

explanation.surface: Someone hopes to prosper eventually once they have crossed a river in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: BE and L join and then straddle FAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something befalls a person when it happens to them, usually something unwelcome.

clue.text: Deliver post, including notes identifying roof timber

indicators.note: including something means taking it inside, so the pair of words holds the notes

parts.note: to deliver someone from a thing is to rid them of it
G and E are musical notes
a post or upright stake is a pole

explanation.surface: A postal worker drops off mail containing notes about the roof beams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliver post' sounds like a postman's job; post is a wooden upright and deliver means free.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridgepole is the horizontal beam along the apex of a roof or tent.

clue.text: Apply pressure to withdraw from specialist

indicators.note: to withdraw from a thing is to leave it, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: an expert is a specialist
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Someone pressures a specialist into pulling out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apply pressure' reads as the definition, but the definition is just 'Apply' and pressure is P.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert force or influence is to apply it, bringing it to bear on something.

clue.text: US composer defending old times in country dwelling

indicators.note: defending something means standing round it, so the composer's name encloses the rest

parts.note: John Cage was an American avant-garde composer
O is the abbreviation for old
T is time, so times gives two of them

explanation.surface: An American composer stands up for bygone days in his rural home.
explanation.definitionFit: A cottage is a small house, typically found in a village or out in the countryside.

clue.text: Water down cement mix used by inspector

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector
lute is a clay or cement compound used to seal joints

explanation.surface: A building inspector checks the cement mixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mix' looks like an anagram signal, but lute is a mixture used as cement.
explanation.definitionFit: To dilute a liquid is to weaken it by adding water, the literal sense of thinning it out.

clue.text: Intelligence of supporter on good terms with current head

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
to be in with someone is to be friendly with them
I is the physics symbol for electric current
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness names and Sheerness

explanation.surface: A fan who gets on well with the current boss shows good sense.
explanation.walkthrough: Supporter suggests a fan, but it is the undergarment.
explanation.definitionFit: Braininess is the quality of being clever, the same as mental ability or intelligence.

clue.text: Unrealistic hopes of rooks in flight?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: daydreams with no chance of coming true
second, whimsical meaning: chess rooks, also called castles, flying through the sky

explanation.walkthrough: Rooks seem to be the black birds, but in chess the rook is also called a castle; the question mark flags the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Building castles in the air is an idiom for fanciful plans or dreams that will never be realised.

clue.text: Duck coming across large person wielding spadelike tool

indicators.note: coming across something here means stretching over it, so the person goes round the letter

parts.note: someone using a shovel is a shoveler
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A duck meets a big man digging with a spade.
explanation.definitionFit: The shoveller is a dabbling duck named for its broad, spoon-shaped bill.

clue.text: Land due to turbulence? That's knotty

indicators.note: turbulence is violent disturbance, so the preceding letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pilot asks whether a turbulent landing is due, a tricky problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Due to' reads as 'because of', but all three words are the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nodulated is covered in small lumps or nodules, the way wood is knotty with knots.

clue.text: He painted a dancer and extremely old violin, originally

indicators.note: originally hints at something put in an original, novel way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so only the outermost letters of the next word are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of old
taken as written

explanation.surface: An artist painted a dancer beside an ancient fiddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' looks like a first-letter signal for violin; it is the anagram signal, and the whole word violin is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo da Vinci was the Renaissance artist who painted the Mona Lisa and The Last Supper.

clue.text: Where fish may be kept, as in part of opera

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in an opera
qua is Latin-derived for 'as' or 'in the capacity of'

explanation.surface: Fish swim in a set designed for an opera scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquaria, the Latin plural of aquarium, are glass tanks in which fish are housed and displayed.

clue.text: Where two gentlemen were putting up an old cleric

indicators.note: in a down clue putting something up means writing it upwards, bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
O is the abbreviation for old
Rev is short for Reverend, a cleric's title

explanation.surface: Two gentlemen were giving lodging to an elderly priest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting up' suggests hosting a guest; Shakespeare's comedy is The Two Gentlemen of Verona.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare set his early comedy The Two Gentlemen of Verona in that Italian city.

clue.text: Young male wolf, perhaps, meeting a Trojan queen

parts.note: a young male wolf, or fox or lion, could be called a he-cub
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wolf cub encounters an ancient queen of Troy.
explanation.definitionFit: Hecuba was the wife of King Priam of Troy in Greek legend and Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: Valediction from a girl at Brussels

parts.note: taken as written
Di, short for Diana, is a girl's name
Brussels is the seat of the European Union

explanation.surface: A young woman working in Brussels says her farewells.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is the French goodbye, used in English as a formal parting word or farewell.

clue.text: Unexpected role Garland's taken on — a siren

indicators.note: something unexpected turns out differently, so the letters come out in another order

parts.note: taken as written
a lei is a Hawaiian flower garland

explanation.surface: Judy Garland accepts a surprising part playing a seductress.
explanation.walkthrough: Garland's capital suggests Judy Garland, the actress; here it is just a wreath of flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lorelei is the legendary Rhine maiden whose singing lured boatmen to their doom, a classic siren.

clue.text: Suppressing anger, see water flowing through Nantes

indicators.note: suppressing means pressing down on top, so in this down clue the second word sits above the first

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
ire is anger

explanation.surface: Someone holding back their temper watches the river pass through a French city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Loire is France's longest river, reaching the Atlantic just beyond the city of Nantes.

clue.text: Search jazz group, missing nothing

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so that letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a combo is a small jazz band
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone hunts for a jazz band that has gone absent.
explanation.definitionFit: To comb an area is to search it thoroughly, as a comb's teeth go through hair.

clue.text: Source of heating abandoned by British tanker

indicators.note: being abandoned by something means it leaves, so that letter goes

parts.note: a boiler heats water for a house
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A British oil tanker has had its heating fail.
explanation.definitionFit: An oiler is a ship that carries oil fuel, a tanker used especially for refuelling other vessels.

clue.text: Concentrated way we count decimally: it's very easy at first

parts.note: counting in base ten means counting in tens

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of each preceding word

parts.note: the first letters of it's, very and easy

explanation.surface: A teacher reassures pupils that counting in base ten is simple.
explanation.definitionFit: Intensive work is concentrated, packing a great deal of effort into a short time.

clue.text: Fish markets principally in Scottish island, and German one

parts.note: Barra is an island in the Outer Hebrides

indicators.note: principally means chiefly, so only the chief, opening letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of markets
und is German for and
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Fish markets on a Scottish island are dominated by one German trader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish markets' reads as one phrase, but Fish alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The barramundi is a large Australian and Asian sea perch, prized as a food fish.

clue.text: Sounds made by seagulls in stable yard

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the cries of gulls
second meaning: a row of stables round a yard, now often homes

explanation.surface: Gulls are crying around the stables.
explanation.definitionFit: A gull's cry is a mew, plural for several; and a London mews was originally a yard of stables.
